text:
maria: Heads-up: deploy-bot scheduled a maintenance window for 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC to roll runtime v1.12.3 -> v1.13.0 across hosted and dedicated. Affects inference control plane and dedicated pinning flow. ETA ~2h.

deploy-bot: [automated] maintenance scheduled by maria for 2026-06-15T02:00:00Z. Affected: hosted API, Dedicated pools (may show brief 503s during node drains). Canaries enabled.

chris: Thanks. Can we pin Dedicated customers still on 1.12.3 automatically? Some customers requested no auto-upgrade.

maria: Yes — default behavior is not to force upgrade for pinned customers. We'll push v1.13 as an available variant and only rotate unpinned pools. For customers who have earlier requested forced upgrade (commit contracts) we'll include them in the reserved pool update.

sre-jen: For oncall scoring: if 5%+ error rate increase or median latency +120ms for >15m we abort and rollback to 1.12.3. Canary thresholds set. Any objections?

chris: Agree. Add CPU/GPU memory OOM metric to abort conditions — seen a spike in model loaders last time.

sre-jen: Good call — adding OOMs and stability errors (worker panics) as hard aborts.

pm-sam: Need a short statuspage blurb and an email template for affected customers (dedicated + hosted). Draft below — please edit.

support-alex: I'll take email and customer-targeted Slack DM snippet. Will schedule send at T-24h and T-1h for impacted customers.

maria: Paste proposed statuspage and email here — keep short and include fallback guidance.

pm-sam: ```Status page (planned incident):
- Summary: Planned runtime upgrade to v1.13.0 for inference runtime; brief request-level disruptions possible.
- Start: 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC
- Duration: ~2 hours (rolling)
- Impact: Possible transient 503s or slight latency increases for some requests; Dedicated customers pinned to v1.12.3 will not be upgraded.
- Mitigation: Canaries + automatic rollbacks on errors; support on standby.
```

pm-sam: ```Customer email subject: Planned maintenance: runtime upgrade (2026-06-15)
Body:
Hi [Customer name],
We will perform a planned runtime upgrade in our inference platform on 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC. The upgrade improves throughput and memory efficiency.
During a rolling update some requests may return 503 or see higher latency for brief periods. Dedicated customers pinned to a specific runtime will not be upgraded unless you opted in.
Actions for you: no action required. If you require zero disruption, reply and we can schedule a maintenance freeze or a private upgrade window.
Support: support@redwood.ai or reply to this email.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops
```

chris: Small tweak — add explicit note about function/tool-calling fallbacks: "If you rely on streaming or function-calling latency-sensitive flows, expect brief stalls; consider increasing client-side retries to 3 with exponential backoff for T+30m."

pm-sam: Updated email and statuspage to include that.

maria: Who will own the statuspage update at T0? I can post initial incident, but want support to own customer replies.

support-alex: I'll publish the statuspage update at T-10m and push email sends. I'll also have CS on standby in #support.

maria: Rollout plan summary: 1) Canary group (2 nodes) -> monitor 30m. 2) Gradual 20% increments across pools with KV cache warmers. 3) If OK, full roll. Pinning: Dedicated pinned pools untouched. 4) If abort -> full rollback to 1.12.3 and mark impacted customers for follow-up.

sre-jen: Logging snippet for the rollback trigger, adding to runbook: ```if (error_rate_delta >= 0.05 || median_latency_delta >= 120 || oom_count >= 1) { abort_rollout(); notify_oncall(); }```

chris: Also ensure release notes mention quantization kernel changes and a note to model owners about re-validation of long-context prompts.

pm-sam: Release notes bullet added to the draft.

maria: Final ask: anyone able to run preflight smoke for dedicated staging pools at T-6h? Need a quick end-to-end test: chat + streaming + embeddings.

sre-jen: I'll run smoke tests at T-6h and post results here.

support-alex: I'll queue the email and customer DM sends and create a small FAQ snippet for CS.

maria: Great — last item: any SLA exceptions we need to pre-authorize for enterprise customers who require credits for maintenance? We have a small list that gets 10% credit for scheduled downtime >1h.

support-alex: I'll pull the list and prepare personalized notes.

maria: Perfect. Thanks everyone — I'll start the canary at 02:00 UTC and post live updates in this thread. :rocket:
